races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Colliers Quay
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and style unknown, so tactics on the day will define its chance; trainer McCarthy has one win from nine in the 14-day window and the horse has one placing from one run on similar good ground — capable of hitting the frame if it settles mid-division.

runners_data.name: Coolishael
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, though the STYLE_FIT flag signals it is stretching its natural role; Ross O'Sullivan sends it here on 79 days' rest with two course-distance placed efforts on good ground, and if it gets an uncontested lead it can be very competitive — but it may not dominate as freely as a natural front-runner would.

runners_data.name: Discrete
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose last three runs on good ground have produced three midfield finishes in the double digits; the overcrowded rear has pushed it onto the map closer than it will actually want to race, and with a very recent run five days ago, freshness is not the concern — quality is.

runners_data.name: Lastofthenatives
runners_data.note: Holds a fade-in-finish flag and has a headgear note (h), finishing 11th, 10th and unknown in three good-ground starts — its true station is at the back of the field, but with the rear overcrowded it will end up racing closer than ideal, limiting its scope for a finishing run.

runners_data.name: Minella Post
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a tongue tie, trained by Gibney, who has placed once from eight good-ground starts; sits prominently on the map in a natural position and the extra age and experience over a field of mostly five-year-olds could prove an edge in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Noharmintrying
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with no hurdles form in the data; trainer Howard is in excellent 14-day form (2/3) and that strike rate in a race of unknowns is worth noting — style is listed as unknown, so it could land anywhere in the field.

runners_data.name: Nothintodowithme
runners_data.note: Murphy runner who fades in the finish and has two poor good-ground efforts (8th and unknown) from two starts; tongue tie fitted and with only 10 days' rest, the quick turnaround does not obviously help a horse that has already been struggling to see out its races.

runners_data.name: Sankofa
runners_data.note: Finished 9th on the one similar-going start to its name and carries a fade flag; trainer Kelly has one win from nine in the 14-day window but there is little in this horse's profile to suggest it will reverse that finishing pattern in an 18-runner field.

runners_data.name: Tommy Go Maith
runners_data.note: Has four pulled-up or question-mark finishes in its last five, with the one completed run on good ground resulting in a 16th — the fade flag and a poor overall record make it very hard to trust at any stage of this race.

runners_data.name: Vargas
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner, who has four winners from 37 in the 14-day window — the yard's volume strike rate is low but the trainer's quality of placing is the key factor; finished 5th on its one good-ground start and races as a hold-up type that could benefit if any pace develops.

runners_data.name: Green Grass
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old with two poor good-ground finishes (12th and 13th) and a fade pattern; its true style is hold-up but the overcrowded rear means it will be forced to race further forward than suited — a tough ask in an already competitive maiden.

runners_data.name: Myhero La Colmine
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed four-year-old with no hurdles form available; trainer Gilligan has no wins from nine in the 14-day window, which tempers expectations, but as with all unknown quantities in this field, a well-schooled debutant cannot be fully dismissed.

runners_data.name: Elusive Truce
runners_data.note: A six-year-old making its hurdles debut for Charlie Keegan, who has no winners in the current 14-day window; the age suggests scope for improvement but the total absence of form data makes it impossible to place with any confidence.

runners_data.name: Leva Deva
runners_data.note: Has finished 10th, 14th and unknown in three good-ground runs and carries a fade flag; the horse is a natural hold-up type displaced onto the map in midfield due to overcrowding, and with a trainer (Collins) who has no recent wins, the profile is not encouraging.

runners_data.name: Roll It Roisin
runners_data.note: David Kelly runner with a tongue tie, finishing 7th on its one comparable good-ground start over 20f; races as a hold-up type in its natural position here and could benefit from the extra distance if the race develops any genuine tempo.

runners_data.name: Lexenna
runners_data.note: Three runs of 6th, 7th and 6th across good and soft ground suggest consistent mid-division finishes without the quality to break through; Collins-trained alongside Leva Deva, the 14-day record (0/4) does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Beyond Forgiveness
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Kelly runner with a 6th on good ground as its only hurdles evidence; the unknown style means it could be placed anywhere, and trainer form (1/9 over 14 days) offers a mild positive hook, but the single run tells us very little.

runners_data.name: Don't Tell Paddy
runners_data.note: Unexposed four-year-old for McCarthy with no hurdles form on record; trainer has one win from nine in the 14-day window and the horse is making what appears to be its hurdles debut — outcome entirely unknown, but that cuts both ways in a wide-open maiden.

races.paceDynamic: Coolishael is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner maiden hurdle and, critically, carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting it is already racing out of its natural role — meaning the pace it sets is likely to be measured and controlled rather than scorching. With Coolishael likely to bowl along at a sustainable clip on good ground at Ballinrobe, the tempo will be honest but not punishing, creating a race that plays out in a relatively strung-out, single-file fashion around this tight track. The field holds significantly more hold-up and prominent types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Leva Deva, Lastofthenatives, Green Grass, and Leva Deva are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because the rear is overcrowded, meaning several will be forced to race closer to the pace than they prefer. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested lead with a moderate pace — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently with cover or sit just off the lone leader and pick up efficiently from two out, rather than genuine deep closers who need a strong gallop to peel off the back of the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coolishael Controls Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Coolishael leads at its own pace and no rival applies sustained pressure through the middle miles.
scenarios.body: Coolishael dictates a manageable tempo, getting its own way in front on good ground, and the race becomes a test of jumping fluency and class from the front; horses who can track the leader through the backstraight and pounce from two out have the clearest route to victory.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Coolishael sets a fair pace but one or two prominent trackers travel powerfully and overwhelm it from the third-last.
scenarios.body: With a sustainable gallop set, horses sitting second or third with energy in reserve are ideally positioned to sweep past the leader jumping the last two hurdles; the good ground rewards a clean-jumping, prominent racer who has been saved from early exertion.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected early and the field bunches, giving true hold-up horses a chance to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace collapse from the front would allow the redistibuted hold-up types to come through late, but because most of the nominally mid-field runners are not natural closers, only a handful carry authentic late-finishing form; the scenario depends on horses racing in their correct role for once.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Lands
scenarios.trigger: If one of the multiple lightly raced or unexposed runners (Noharmintrying, Myhero La Colmine, Elusive Truce, Don't Tell Paddy) produces a sharply improved hurdling display on debut or reappearance.
scenarios.body: With several runners having no meaningful hurdles form on record, an unexposed type could bolt up if significantly ahead of its mark; the stable form of Aidan Anthony Howard (T14: 2/3) around Noharmintrying makes that runner the most plausible candidate.

watchPoints.text: Coolishael's front-running role is flagged as out of character (STYLE_FIT=0.90) — watch whether it actually leads from flag fall or allows another runner to push past it early, which would fundamentally reshape the pace dynamic.

With at least five runners tagged as redistributed hold-up types (Discrete, Lastofthenatives, Green Grass, Leva Deva, Nothintodowithme) forced to race closer than suited, watch for a congested mid-pack in the early stages at Ballinrobe's tight track, increasing the risk of interference or jumping errors.

Noharmintrying (trainer Howard, T14 2/3) is completely unexposed — watch for it to be well-backed in the market as a potential dark horse whose lack of form data conceals a significant ability advantage.

Minella Post is the oldest runner at seven and brings more racecourse experience than the predominantly five-year-old field — watch whether its jumping is sharper and more economical than its rivals', which on a good surface could prove decisive in a steadily-run race.

Three runners (Myhero La Colmine, Elusive Truce, Don't Tell Paddy) have no hurdles form whatsoever — watch the market moves for any of these at the off, as unexpected market support for an unexposed type in a race this open is often the only signal available.

races.name: Hollymount Nursing Home Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Manoir De Mirande
runners_data.note: Four-year-old in superb form (three wins in last five, two on this track over this trip on good ground), Gordon Elliott yard operating at 4/37 over 14 days but the horse's own record carries the argument; as the lone front-runner with no credible rival for the lead, STYLE_FIT note means discount if the race shape somehow requires a different position, but here their role is entirely natural.

runners_data.name: O'Grady Cracker
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winners (form 800-11) with Slevin up and course form solid on good ground; a hold-up horse who drops in off a light 21-day break, but the fade-in-finish flag is a real caution — needs a true pace to close into rather than a stolen, slow-tempo win from the front.

runners_data.name: Houndsworth
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for McNiff, 14 days since last run with a 7lb claim for Alan King; form has slipped since a course win (17-654), and sim-going record of just one win from 13 comparable runs makes a winning performance a stretch even if the race sets up for closers.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Prominent racer back just five days after a run — quick turnaround for Flynn's yard (1/23 over 14 days); winless on similar going with a form string of 7R560 suggesting consistency is not a strength, and the short recovery window adds a fitness query rather than a confidence boost.

runners_data.name: Ocean Murphy
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse in form (74-912, two wins at 20f on good ground) for Rothwell and Darragh O'Keeffe; mapped to midfield because the rear is congested, but will likely race further back than the map suggests — the forced positional compromise means the STYLE_FIT discount is relevant if a true hold-up run is needed to win.

runners_data.name: Nile Star
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's four-year-old has a 43-day absence, no wins from five comparable going runs, and a fade-in-finish warning; also carries a redistribution flag meaning its natural closer position is already compromised before the race starts — the accumulation of negatives makes this the hardest horse in the field to construct a winning case for.

races.paceDynamic: Manoir De Mirande is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner handicap hurdle and, with no genuine rival to press them into a contested gallop, Joshua Halford's mount should dictate a measured, controlled pace over the 2m2½f trip on good ground. William F Browne is the only other prominent-style runner in the field, but a modest recent form string (7R560) makes it unlikely they will impose any serious early pressure on Manoir De Mirande. The field nominally holds more hold-up horses than the shape can accommodate — Ocean Murphy and Nile Star are genuine closers pushed into mapped midfield positions because the rear is overcrowded on paper, but their true preference is to race from off the pace, meaning they will be doing their running late from a compressed group. This race shape — a single front-runner controlling a sustainable tempo against a cluster of hold-up types who must make their ground in the straight — favours prominent-to-lead profiles who can conserve energy behind the leader and time their challenge, rather than true deep closers who need a genuine test of stamina to peg them back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Manoir De Mirande Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Manoir De Mirande dictates an uncontested lead at a comfortable pace and kicks clear from the home turn.
scenarios.body: The Elliott-trained four-year-old has won twice over this course and distance on good ground and, given no rival has the will or ability to challenge for the lead, can run the race entirely to their own rhythm; prominent horses who can track the leader get the clearest path to the winner's enclosure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Manoir De Mirande sets a strong-enough gallop that closers can reel them in through the final flight.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong pace would compress the finish and bring the hold-up horses into play, rewarding those with proven form at the trip on good ground; O'Grady Cracker, who has won twice recently, is well-suited if they can produce a finishing burst from behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If William F Browne travels well into contention behind Manoir De Mirande and outstays them from the second-last.
scenarios.body: William F Browne's prominent style means they would be handily placed throughout, and if Manoir De Mirande's advantage is nullified by a testing final climb, a fresh challenger with a recent run (5 days ago) could hit the line with energy; the concern is limited recent form quality makes this a conditional upside.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Staying Grind Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively demanding and the race turns into a stamina test that catches the front-runner cold.
scenarios.body: A collapse by Manoir De Mirande late in the race would theoretically open the door for genuine hold-up horses, but both Ocean Murphy and Nile Star carry redistribution flags and a fade-warning applies to Nile Star, so the scenario depends on horses racing against their best natural conditions; Houndsworth's single course win and modest recent form (17-654) offers a slim each-way profile if everything falls right.

watchPoints.text: Manoir De Mirande must be monitored jumping — if they make an early error and lose their uncontested lead, the entire race shape collapses immediately.
O'Grady Cracker's fade-in-finish flag means watch whether Slevin positions them closer than usual to compensate; if they settle too deep behind a slow pace, their chance evaporates.

Ocean Murphy and Nile Star are both true hold-up horses compressed into midfield by the field composition — if they both attempt to race genuinely from off the pace, the midfield could become congested and cause interference entering the home straight.

William F Browne's five-day turnaround is unusual — watch the betting market for any significant move that would suggest connections have a specific reason for running back so quickly on different ground to their last start.

races.review_reason: style/note conflict — check before trusting notes

races.name: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Goodgollymissholly
runners_data.note: Elliott's 5yo has a strong recent profile on good ground — four from four sim-going runs producing a win and two places — and Jordan Gainford navigates a prominent position naturally; the 38-day break looks straightforward and her 2m-plus hurdle form reads as the most consistent card in the race.

runners_data.name: Amina
runners_data.note: McConnell's 6yo has been placed four times on good ground without winning, and the headgear and 71-day absence warrant monitoring; she wants to be prominent and will look to take up a handy pitch from her wide draw, but her pattern suggests she finds a way to finish second rather than first.

runners_data.name: Clash Gold
runners_data.note: Flood's 7yo is a genuine hold-up horse by style whose true running preference is from the rear, though the density of prominent types in this field means she will likely race closer than ideal; the recent placed effort on good ground is the most relevant form line, but racing out of role in a shape that does not suit is a meaningful discount.

runners_data.name: Cool Native
runners_data.note: Kennedy takes the mount for Elliott's second string here, and Cool Native's three placed finishes on good ground over similar trips establish her stamina credentials clearly; she will press up to be prominent and her 41-day break looks untroubling, though she has yet to win.

runners_data.name: Daphne Blake
runners_data.note: A lightly raced 6yo for Peter Maher with no recorded going or hurdle history to assess, making her a genuine unknown; John Shinnick's low-key booking and the blank form column mean she must be treated with caution until she shows something tangible.

runners_data.name: Doesthatmakesense
runners_data.note: Seymour's 5yo has a flag for fading in finishes and her three runs on good ground have all ended in double-figure placings; she will try to race prominently but has shown nothing to suggest she can sustain that position to the line over this extended trip.

runners_data.name: Free A Minute
runners_data.note: Keegan's 7yo carries a fades-in-finish flag and three poor recent good-ground efforts, and despite a hold-up style she lacks the form substance to be credible even if the pace scenario happened to suit; the 21-day turnaround is quick for a horse running this poorly.

runners_data.name: I Dont Really Care
runners_data.note: Hackett's 5yo has only two runs to assess — a fourth and a well-beaten 14th — and while good ground is in the profile the form is too thin to place much confidence; Daniel King partners a runner that has shown hold-up tendencies but little else.

runners_data.name: Labondance
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins sends out this 5yo for the first time in 286 days, and the heavy ground form from the Curragh over hurdles gives little read on how she will handle good turf; the long layoff is the dominant concern, though Meyler's booking is worth a note if she appears fit in the parade ring.

runners_data.name: Run For Power
runners_data.note: C Byrnes' 6yo has been beaten 6+ lengths in all three good-ground runs and holds a hold-up style that requires more pace than a single front-runner is likely to generate; the 17-day turnaround is brisk and Philip Byrnes' claim does not add enough tactical upside to compensate for the weak form.

runners_data.name: Castle Garden
runners_data.note: Hassett's 4yo has only a single run to reference — a third — and J J Slevin's presence is the main reason to give her a line; lightly raced, unknown on this going, and stepping up significantly in trip, she is best treated as an unknown quantity with potential upside rather than a calculable factor.

runners_data.name: Gunner Girl
runners_data.note: S G Carey's 4yo has finished 13th and 7th in her two good-ground starts and her hold-up style requires a strong pace that this race is unlikely to produce; the 23-day break is routine but nothing in the form suggests she can bridge a wide gap to the principals.

runners_data.name: Ronnie's Rascal
runners_data.note: Mullins' 4yo is the confirmed pace-setter and Brian Hayes will slot her out in front on a track where controlling the fractions is a genuine asset; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that she is operating slightly out of her most comfortable role under pressure from prominent rivals, but as the lone leader she gets first run on everything and that is a meaningful position advantage.

races.paceDynamic: Ronnie's Rascal is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one horse likely to dictate, she sets a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m6½f on good ground at Ballinrobe — a track that rewards jumping fluency and stamina rather than raw speed. Goodgollymissholly, Cool Native, Amina, and Doesthatmakesense are all prominent-style runners who will want to be close to the pace, creating a relatively congested mid-division rather than any serious early pressure on the leader. Clash Gold is a genuine hold-up type that the field density pushes toward midfield rather than her natural rear position, meaning the true back-markers are thin on the ground. This shape — a single uncontested leader setting an honest but unforced pace in a 13-runner mares maiden over an extended trip — strongly favours prominent racers who travel close to the tempo and can grind out the finish, with any late finisher needing the pace to collapse to have a realistic chance. The field holds more prominent types than can all get their natural position; Ronnie's Rascal is best-placed to lead, with Goodgollymissholly and Cool Native most likely to secure the spots immediately behind her.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ronnie's Rascal dictates an uncontested pace and the race is run at an even tempo throughout
scenarios.body: Ronnie's Rascal sets fractions that suit the chasers and the contest becomes a stamina grind from the home turn, rewarding horses who have tracked the pace comfortably. Prominent runners who have been close enough throughout inherit the race as the leader ties up or holds on, with Good Good Going stamina being the key discriminator.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Fades, Midfield Striker
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is deceptively fast and Ronnie's Rascal's lead evaporates approaching the final flight
scenarios.body: The front-runners burn each other's cover and the race opens up for a horse who has been stalking just off the pace and picks up as others weaken. Goodgollymissholly's consistent good-ground form and Amina's placed record on similar going make them the likeliest beneficiaries of a modest fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a true late-run opportunity
scenarios.body: Clash Gold, the sole genuine hold-up type in the field, would need the pace to be far more punishing than the single-leader setup suggests, making this shape less likely given she is naturally pushed forward. Should conditions align, her recent placed effort on good ground is the most relevant piece of form, and Labondance's stamina-heavy hurdle profile could also get involved from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Lottery, Lightly Raced
scenarios.trigger: If the race degenerates into a messy affair with jumping errors or falls disrupting the anticipated shape
scenarios.body: Daphne Blake and Castle Garden, both lightly raced and form unknowns, carry potential upside if the field thins unexpectedly and class counts for less than a clear round. In a fractured race an unexposed type can inherit a position they would not otherwise reach, and J J Slevin's experience on Castle Garden represents the most credible dark-horse claim.

watchPoints.text: Goodgollymissholly's good-ground form profile (4/4 runs, one win, two places) is the standout data point in this field — watch whether Jordan Gainford gets her locked onto Ronnie's Rascal's girth early, as that position could be decisive in a stamina grind.

Ronnie's Rascal may face more pressure from Cool Native and Amina than the lone-leader framing suggests — if either tracks her aggressively in the first mile the early gallop could quicken beyond what Mullins' filly can sustain on this demanding 2m6½f trip.

Labondance's 286-day absence for Emmet Mullins is the single biggest fitness question in the race; watch her closely in the parade ring and pre-race canter for signs of condition, as Mullins does occasionally produce first-time-out winners off long breaks.

Clash Gold's redistribution to midfield means she will not be racing from her natural position — if the pace is genuine she could stay on into contested placings, but punters should not assume she will produce her best form from a position she does not naturally occupy.

Castle Garden (Slevin/Hassett) and Daphne Blake (Shinnick/Maher) are both form blanks on this going and trip — either could improve dramatically or disappoint; their behaviour at the start and first few flights will be the earliest read on whether they are worth following through the race.

races.name: Jerry McDonnell Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner; Emmet Mullins sends her here fresh (31 days) with a tongue-tie and a cheekpiece, and her recent Good-ground form over staying trips is solid — she holds the key tactical position in this race, though her STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is being used more aggressively than usual and a lack of finishing kick could cost her late.

runners_data.name: Joshua Chamberlain
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who stays well and has winning form on soft and good; Eoghan Finegan (5lb claim) takes the ride for a trainer with a 1/7 14-day strike rate, and his ability to sit close to the pace without being consumed by it is his main asset over this staying trip.

runners_data.name: Gerrys Wish
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is a major booking for Gordon Elliott's five-year-old, who has been remarkably consistent in placed form on Good ground (4 places from 4 similar-going starts); a hold-up style suits this shape only if a clear run materialises in the straight, but the quality of the trainer-jockey combination demands respect.

runners_data.name: The Vegas Raider
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for K A Heffernan who ran just 14 days ago and showed a placed effort over 2m2f on Good; his tongue-tie and visor combination is retained, but a patchy recent record including a couple of non-completions means trust is limited even if the style fits a late-running scenario.

runners_data.name: Ancient Myth
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for a small County Clare yard with no 14-day runners, so trainer data is thin; cheekpieces are on, and while he won once on soft going, his last four Good-ground results read 10-13-10-12 — it is hard to construct a case for him in this competitive 19-runner field.

runners_data.name: Barryroe Madam
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up mare who has struggled for consistency, her best Good-ground effort being a fourth from 24f at Galway; the headgear note (h) and a 32-day break suggest she is fresh, but her form over this sort of trip is mixed and she offers little pace-map advantage.

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Gavin Cromwell who boasts a 7/27 14-day trainer strike rate — one of the strongest in this field; he was placed just 15 days ago and his tongue-tie is retained, and his ability to sit close to Giorgia Rose without burning petrol is his principal weapon in this shape.

runners_data.name: It's Time Again
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has repeatedly tackled Good ground over 22f trips without winning in his last four completions; the 3lb claimer Liam McKenna takes the ride, but the form string of 0PF89 is concerning and he is unlikely to exert meaningful influence on the race outcome.

runners_data.name: Ballyminnion Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged as a fader in the finish, which is a significant concern over 2m6½f; four runs on Good ground and no placed effort from those trips tells its own story, and he has the lowest ceiling of the mid-rated horses in this field.

runners_data.name: Ranger Billy
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has shown some promise placing twice in Good-going handicaps at this sort of trip; J J Slevin is a high-quality booking for the Heffernan yard, and while he ran only 14 days ago and is carrying 153lbs, his ability to sit handy gives him a structural advantage.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Soldier
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse returning from 1,038 days off — an extraordinary absence — for David Richard Barry; his two Good-ground runs in history came on Headford going and he fades in finishes, making it extremely difficult to see how this campaign restart translates to a competitive showing here regardless of map position.

runners_data.name: Chanceitlucky
runners_data.note: Naturally operates from the rear, but because the field is overloaded with hold-up types, he is mapped to midfield — a position that is not his comfort zone; his trainer Adrian Murray has a 1/2 14-day record, he ran 14 days ago, and the tongue-tie is on, but the STYLE_FIT discount is real.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: A five-year-old by John McConnell's yard who ran just nine days ago and is a natural hold-up performer; his best form is a second and two fourths on Good ground but all at shorter trips, and the extra yardage of 2m6½f is an open question — his true rear-running style is squeezed into midfield by the field's composition.

runners_data.name: Phildante
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 24f on Good ground and has placed twice from hold-up positions; Joshua Halford claims 7lbs, which is meaningful weight relief, and he is one of the more interesting horses among the redistributed group — though racing forward of his natural position, his stamina profile genuinely suits this distance.

runners_data.name: Tawny Lea
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a fade flag, four runs on Good ground and not a single placed effort from those; absent 31 days and has no form string beyond four poor results — she is among the least likely to factor here even in the most generous scenario.

runners_data.name: Princess Felicia
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has placed twice on Good ground over 20f, both for Peter Smithers; the fade-in-finish flag is a concern over the extra yardage here, and her form line of 2-3-14-10-9 in those Good-ground runs shows she has capability at the right end of the field but cannot be relied upon to sustain it.

runners_data.name: Tantrum Boy
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which is notable this close to the off; a hold-up type flagged as a fader, with no wins on Good ground and his only in-the-frame efforts coming on Soft — the surface switch and lack of a confirmed rider make him highly speculative.

runners_data.name: But What About Me
runners_data.note: Returns from a 500-day absence for Barry T Murphy, so fitness is a serious question mark; the fade flag and a career record that shows seven and eight on Good ground at relevant trips suggest even a race-fit version of this horse would struggle in this company.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner
runners_data.note: Absent 327 days and returning for Norman Lee with a fade-in-finish warning; 11 from 11 in Good-ground finishes tells a bleak story, and while he once placed over 22f on Good, there is no realistic basis to argue he can bounce back from this layoff into a 19-runner competitive handicap hurdle.

races.paceDynamic: Giorgia Rose is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop over 2m6½f on good ground — a trip that rewards stamina but does not automatically punish the leader when the pace is honest rather than suicidal. Behind her, Joshua Chamberlain, My Good Pal, It's Time Again and Ranger Billy will push to hold prominent positions, creating a competitive chase pack but not a pace war at the front. Gerrys Wish, The Vegas Raider and Ancient Myth are the most credible hold-up operators, though the field is so saturated with horses mapped to midfield and rear that many — including Chanceitlucky, Fine Print, Phildante and Blackwater Soldier — are genuine hold-up types displaced into the midfield band because the map cannot accommodate them all at the back; of those, Chanceitlucky and Fine Print are most likely to actively try to press toward prominent positions given their natural style. The dominant tactical verdict is clear: with a single unchallenged leader setting a sustainable clip and the bulk of the field crowding midfield, horses with a prominent-to-midfield profile who can travel smoothly within the first five and produce a measured late effort are best positioned, while true closers face a traffic problem and must produce something exceptional to thread through a congested field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Giorgia Rose Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Giorgia Rose is allowed to lead without serious early pressure and sets a gallop sustainable enough to hold on at 2m6½f.
scenarios.body: Giorgia Rose settles into her own rhythm from the front, the field strings out behind her, and the combination of a honest-but-not-killing pace and good ground means stamina rather than turn of foot settles matters; horses who can travel prominently and pounce without needing a gap are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack of Joshua Chamberlain, My Good Pal and Ranger Billy press Giorgia Rose into a stronger gallop and the race becomes a sustained test of stamina from the front.
scenarios.body: The increased tempo filters out hold-up horses who never get into range, and the race is decided between those who have been travelling prominently throughout; good-ground form and stamina over this sort of trip become critical filters.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the prominent runners exhaust each other, leaving a gap for a hold-up horse to come through late.
scenarios.body: Gerrys Wish or The Vegas Raider, operating from just off the pace, find a clear run approaching the last and reel in a tiring leader; this scenario is partially discounted because several of the horses mapped to the rear are redistributed types who may not settle as true hold-up operators.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If traffic is unexpectedly clear in the straight and a midfield tracker finds a clear passage while the front group ties up.
scenarios.body: A horse like Chanceitlucky or Fine Print — true hold-up types squeezed into midfield — happens to find room and runs on past fading rivals; this scenario carries the lowest probability because it requires multiple conditions to align and both horses are racing out of natural role.

watchPoints.text: Giorgia Rose has unchallenged control of the pace but carries 166lbs and has not won in her last five starts — watch whether the prominent pack (My Good Pal, Joshua Chamberlain) allows her any daylight or begins to crowd her from the second circuit.

The field contains at least six horses returning from layoffs of 14 days or less, and three from over 300 days — watch for interference and crowding when the field compacts approaching the second-last hurdle, particularly involving the redistributed midfield group.

Gerrys Wish with Jack Kennedy is the highest-profile jockey-trainer combination in the race; watch how Kennedy positions him leaving the back straight — if he is not in the first eight at the top of the home turn, a winning run from the hold-up position becomes very difficult in this field size.
Tantrum Boy has no jockey confirmed in the data — watch for a late withdrawal or a significant booking change that could shift how the midfield traffic develops.

Phildante (7lb claim, recent win over 24f on Good) is the most interesting of the redistributed hold-up horses — watch whether Joshua Halford attempts to push him forward early to reclaim a more natural prominent berth, which could significantly alter the race shape behind Giorgia Rose.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Addragoole
runners_data.note: OR 140 class runner with a win at 17f on Good and excellent similar-going record (2W5P from 9 runs); wears headgear and travels prominently — Keith Donoghue keeps him close to the pace, making him the key danger to Runcok if the front-runner is to be overhauled.|

runners_data.name: Ma Jacks Hill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner with a win at 20f on Good; a genuine prominent racer by style but bumped into midfield here because the forward slots are taken — racing out of role tempers expectations, though the 16-day turnaround and a lively juvenile record at this trip keep him in the mix.|

runners_data.name: Runcok
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the field; JJ Slevin's patient handling of the tempo on Good ground over this 2m1f trip is the defining tactical factor, and his one win came at 16f on Good — whether he sees out the extra furlongs under a chase-style test is the key question.|

runners_data.name: Bowensonfire
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's mount is a pure hold-up horse who has placed twice in similar Good-ground chases (2nd at 18f, 3rd at 17f); the LR flag of just 2 days is worth monitoring for freshness, though the Elliott yard are running him knowingly and he needs genuine pace to exploit his finishing run.|

runners_data.name: Bunting
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained 6-year-old with a modest recent record (0W1P from 8 similar-going runs); a natural prominent horse pushed back into midfield by this race shape, so he is unlikely to get his favoured berth — Bunting's chance is conditional on the race developing in a way that lets him into contention from a position he doesn't naturally occupy.|

runners_data.name: Jazzy Matty
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 145 and best similar-going record (2W6P from 11 runs); races prominently and has course/distance profile that fits this shape well — Danny Gilligan can slot him just off Runcok and he finished placed at 16f and 20f on Good, making the 2m1f trip a comfortable enough ask.|

races.paceDynamic: Runcok is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to dispute the lead from the outset, he should be able to control the tempo at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m1f at Ballinrobe. Addragoole and Jazzy Matty will press from a prominent position, while Bowensonfire is the field's only true hold-up horse and will be ridden for late cover. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the pace map can accommodate — Ma Jacks Hill and Bunting are genuine prominent racers but are mapped to midfield because Runcok and Addragoole are more likely to secure those forward berths. A lone, uncontested front-runner dictating on Good ground over this trip at a controlled clip strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and outstay rivals in the straight, rather than pure closers waiting off a falsely-run or pressured pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Runcok Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Runcok leads unchallenged and sets a measured pace that suits prominent trackers over the final two fences.
scenarios.body: Runcok dictates from the front at a controlled tempo, and horses who travel close to the pace — Addragoole and Jazzy Matty — are best placed to pick him off or follow him home in a stamina-test run at an honest but not brutal gallop. Bowensonfire's hold-up style means he may not generate enough momentum late unless the pace quickens sharply, leaving the race to the prominent profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Increases, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Ma Jacks Hill or Bunting force a more pressured tempo from mid-race, raising the overall gallop and leaving the front-runners vulnerable.
scenarios.body: A faster-run race stretches the field and Bowensonfire, the genuine hold-up horse ridden by Jack Kennedy, gets the strong pace he needs to motor past tired rivals on the run-in. Addragoole, with Good-ground form credentials and a return to a similar trip to his best win, could also pick up well if the leaders tie up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just lively enough to bunch the field without fully stretching it, producing a tight multi-horse finish at the last.
scenarios.body: In a compressed, tactical affair Jazzy Matty's prominent profile and proven Good-ground form (2W at similar conditions) allow him to stay competitive through the final fences, and Addragoole's OR 140 class asserts in a race that rewards quality over pure galloping ability. Ma Jacks Hill, a natural prominent racer forced wider in the pack, could find daylight late if the field concertinas.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Runcok's jumping breaks down or he is asked to go too fast too soon and capitulates at the final obstacles.
scenarios.body: A rare scenario where the pace genuinely collapses up front and Bowensonfire, or a revived Bunting racing out of his optimal role, swoops past a laboured leader late. This shape is unlikely given Runcok's previous winning form on Good ground and the steadiness expected from JJ Slevin in the saddle.

watchPoints.text: Runcok's jumping under JJ Slevin is the fulcrum of the entire race — if he flukes or fumbles at a fence mid-race the whole shape collapses and closers like Bowensonfire move into contention immediately.

Bowensonfire's 2-day turnaround (LR:2d) is unusually short for a chaser; watch the pre-race paddock to assess freshness and whether Jack Kennedy is instructed to drop him in conservatively or chase the pace.

Ma Jacks Hill and Bunting are both natural prominent types who cannot both get their preferred position — watch the first fence to see who concedes ground and who edges forward, as the loser of that early negotiation is racing fully out of role.

Jazzy Matty at OR 145 carries top weight (156lbs) and is the highest-rated horse in the field — if Cian Collins's runner travels fluently in behind Runcok in the first mile, he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race at the second-last.

Good ground is consistent throughout the card at Ballinrobe — no going deterioration expected, meaning all runners are likely to perform to their going preferences and no tactical surprise is anticipated from an altered surface.

races.name: Corrib Oil Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Donnie Devito
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Ross O'Sullivan who has hit the frame in five of his last six starts on good ground, but his 7th-of-22 last time at Killarney is a mild flag and Ballinrobe's relatively flat finish suits closers less than sharp tracks; 24 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Fou De Toi
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained five-year-old whose natural inclination is to race prominently, but with several other prominent types in this field he is liable to be shuffled further back than he wants; his good-ground figures are modest (0W1P from six) and Daniel King takes over in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Jeroboam Machin
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins runner who has placed at Gowran and Killarney on good ground over comparable trips and is naturally inclined to press the pace; Donagh Meyler is a positive booking and this horse's course-and-distance profile makes him one of the most relevantly placed runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Kevin's Pride
runners_data.note: J J Slevin rides this John McConnell-trained seven-year-old who owns two wins and two places from nine starts on good-to-soft or better, but he is a horse who wants to be prominent and in this traffic he is unlikely to achieve that naturally; the 45-day absence and tongue strap are worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Maverick Mack
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old is the most lightly exposed runner here having accumulated incomplete results (unseated, pulled-up, brought-down), making him genuinely hard to assess; 78 days off is notable and his only win came on heavy at Navan over a much shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Mickie Angel
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's consistent eight-year-old has placed in three of his last five on good or good-to-firm and races prominently; Sean Flanagan is a strong jockey booking and the 16-day turnaround is not a concern given the horse's regular campaign pattern.

runners_data.name: Rusty Harkness
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old arrives on the back of a win at Punchestown (good, 2m) followed by second at Fairyhouse, both on similar going to today, making him the best-credentialled runner in terms of recent good-ground form at a comparable level; Darragh O'Keeffe continues in the saddle and the step up to 2m7½f is his only open query.

runners_data.name: Slurricane
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue's mount is the race's confirmed pace-setter, but his form figures (7-8-6-10-4 in recent starts, all short of this trip) invite serious questions about whether he can sustain the lead for 2m7½f; his front-running role is a tactical fact, his ability to last home is very much not.

runners_data.name: Jolie Jewel
runners_data.note: Phillip Enright partners this Bri an McMahon-trained mare who has placed in seven of her last 14 starts on good ground, consistently finishing into the frame without winning; a hold-up ride at Ballinrobe is structurally disadvantaged in a race expected to be run at a controlled tempo.

races.paceDynamic: Slurricane is the sole confirmed front runner and, on good ground over 2m7½f at Ballinrobe, should bowl along at a manageable, rhythm-dictating tempo without any serious early challenge to his position. Jeroboam Machin, Mickie Angel, and Rusty Harkness are the prominent types most likely to track him at close quarters, with Rusty Harkness — who won over 2m at Punchestown on good last time — best placed of those to capitalise on a predictable gallop. The field contains more naturally prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate: Fou De Toi and Kevin's Pride are genuine up-with-the-pace operators who will be squeezed back from their preferred positions, meaning they will race out of role and their chances are structurally discounted. With a single, uncontested pacer setting a fair but honest gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses who can sit in the first three and jump fluently — prominent stalkers who conserve energy behind Slurricane before pressing from three out are the clear beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slurricane Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Slurricane bowls along uncontested and the race is run at a steady-to-fair pace that compresses the field.
scenarios.body: Slurricane sets a rhythm that suits horses sitting prominently just behind him, and the race turns into a jumping contest from three out where fluency and fitness decide it; Rusty Harkness and Jeroboam Machin are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to string the field out and the leaders tie each other up from two out.
scenarios.body: Donnie Devito and Jolie Jewel, having travelled through the race from the rear, get a flat enough finish at Ballinrobe to arrive with momentum; this scenario depends on Slurricane over-committing, which his recent form does not particularly suggest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Jeroboam Machin or Mickie Angel apply more pressure to Slurricane from the outset, lifting the pace and turning it into a test of stamina at the front.
scenarios.body: A stronger-run race over this extended trip on good ground filters out the hold-up horses and rewards whoever jumps best in the lead group; Mickie Angel's consistency in placing (three thirds from five recent starts) and Jeroboam Machin's course experience make them the likeliest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors reshuffle the front group mid-race and an unexpected horse finds daylight.
scenarios.body: Maverick Mack, trained by Gordon Elliott and returning after 78 days off, represents the lightly-exposed wildcard who could benefit from a messy race; this scenario is low-probability given the clean going and the likely controlled nature of the race.

watchPoints.text: Slurricane has led every race he has entered but his five most recent finishes are all outside the top six — watch whether Keith Donoghue attempts to steady him and conserve fuel, or whether the horse consumes himself in front.

Rusty Harkness steps up significantly in trip today having won over 2m on good at Punchestown; if the pace is truly honest this 2m7½f distance could stretch him, and any sign of laboured jumping from three out would be telling.

Fou De Toi and Kevin's Pride are both natural prominent racers who are likely to find themselves racing in unfamiliar midfield positions given the crowded pace profile — watch their early body language to assess whether they are travelling or fighting their riders.

Maverick Mack returns after 78 days for Gordon Elliott having accumulated three non-completions in his last six starts — a clean round of jumping today will tell us far more about this horse's current wellbeing than any form reading can.

Jolie Jewel has posted 14 placings from 15 starts on good ground without winning — she fills frames relentlessly but Ballinrobe's flat finish is unlikely to provide the late surge she needs if the pace is controlled.
